source.title: How Does Overparameterization Affect Features?
source.authors: A. Duzgun; Samy Jelassi; Yuanzhi Li

record.file_problem: none; full paper text supplied, including appendices
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether width changes trained networks' held-out performance and whether adding or comparing feature sets changes it, using linear probes and feature residuals rather than the original versions' methods.
record.gate_note: Reports measured training/test accuracy by width (Table 2), linear-probe test accuracy on concatenated versus wide features (Figure 3), and test-accuracy changes after appending feature residuals (Figures 4, 10; Appendix D). FSE values concern feature reconstruction rather than the claim's train/test error gap and are not rows. The synthetic toy task measures signal-vector learning, not one of V1–V8.
record.test_reason: The study measures width-dependent representations and predictive accuracy, but does not establish widening beyond a zero-training-error threshold, as V2 requires. Its high-width/low-width terminology is defined relative to model size rather than an empirically identified interpolation threshold. Feature-span and residual-probe results address a different question. No other version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors conclude that sufficiently narrow networks learn distinct features and their concatenations fail to recover high-width feature spans or linear-probe accuracy. High-width residuals improve narrow-feature performance, whereas narrow-feature residuals do not improve high-width performance. The synthetic mechanism illustrates only part of this asymmetry.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies width-scaled trained networks, feature-span regression and linear-probe feature performance; it does not test the original claim's label memorization or compare its listed recipes. Vision models use SGD with momentum, tuned weight decay and learning rate, standard augmentation, dropout=0.1, 300 epochs and batch size 128; NLP models use AdamW with tuned weight decay and learning rate, 30 epochs. The feature-probe experiments use 40 or 80 epochs and ensure training loss is constant.
record.method_sensitivity: Feature-span error is sensitive to whether task training/test data or shuffled mixed data are used in regression for vision models; authors report a notable validation-test disparity for regular regression and a reduced gap for shuffled regression. Width also changes reported feature performance; NLP shows no notable natural-model performance difference between low- and high-width networks, as described in Appendix A.2.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 2 reports increasing test accuracy with width, alongside increasing training accuracy. It does not identify a zero-training-error threshold.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under the tested regularized training recipes, wider ResNet-18 and VGG-16 models on CIFAR-10 and modified Transformers on MNLI attain higher training and test accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: For sufficiently narrow constituent networks, parameter-count-matched feature concatenations have lower linear-probe test accuracy than a single high-width network.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Concatenating independently trained narrow-network representations does not recover the predictive performance of a single high-width representation in these settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Appending high-width residual features improves narrow-feature probes. Residual-only probes exceed random-feature baselines for ResNet and VGG, while the Transformer result is slightly lower.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: High-width representations contain predictive information unavailable to concatenated narrow representations; residual-only usefulness varies by architecture and task.

record.problems: The authors focus on small-scale settings because FSE is computationally expensive. Main FSE findings use validation errors; test-error trends are said to be consistent, but vision validation/test disparities are acknowledged and linked to data dependence. They report removing 12 of 5120 VGG features whose test errors exceeded 5 in one random-network analysis. NLP models have no notable performance difference between low and high width, and their embedding layer was removed with pretrained hidden representations used as inputs.
record.rows_left_out: No independently reported numeric values for plotted linear-probe accuracies are stated in the text; figure-only values are included as figure_only rows. FSE curves and the synthetic-task signal-vector learning findings were omitted because they do not measure the claim versions' target outcomes. No separately numeric text is supplied for the Figure 4c/4d comparison that adding low-width residuals to high-width features does not improve performance; this is stated in prose but is not a row measuring any listed version.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label generalization under the same recipe, and chance-level held-out performance with random labels.
Test-error behavior when widening beyond an established zero-training-error threshold. The experiments also use explicit regularization and different architectures from the original setting.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Controlled comparisons of adaptive optimizers with SGD, including tuning-dependent differences.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets or adapted training recipes.
Dropout interventions and their effects across training-set sizes, dropout strengths, or augmentation regimes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, its association with generalization gaps, and comparisons with other measures.
Removal of highly memorized examples versus random removal and subsequent test accuracy.

record.verdict_notes: The Appendix A.2 statement about no notable NLP performance difference concerns an earlier setup retaining embeddings. The reported MNLI experiments remove embeddings and use pretrained hidden representations; Table 2 shows width-dependent accuracy in that modified setup. States of cannot_determine here mean the rows do not establish a listed version, not that their reported outcomes are unreadable.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization in the same architecture and recipe.
A one-hidden-layer ReLU width sweep beyond interpolation and its test-error curve.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and the role of local connectivity.
Large versus small batch size under controlled epoch or adaptive recipes.
Dropout versus no dropout and its regime-dependent effect.
Magnitude-aware sharpness or other measured properties tracking train-test gap.
Removal of memorized training examples and its effect on held-out accuracy.
